correctness.rationale: Unrolling the lateral Euclidean cone yields independent normalized slant radii R,S with density 2r and folded angular separation Delta uniform [0,alpha], alpha=pi*kappa<pi; D^2/L^2=R^2+S^2-2RS cosDelta. Increasing in Delta and strict convexity in (R,S) place maximum at radial corners: two apex-rim ordered contacts for alpha<pi/3, one rim-rim contact for alpha>pi/3, all three at equality. Radial-angle rescalings give a 2D triangular integral 4tan(alpha)/(3alpha) below, 3D simplex integral 2/(3alpha sin^2(alpha/2)cos(alpha/2)) above; at alpha=pi/3 they add to 28/(pi*sqrt3). Almost-sure monotone coupling in kappa yields stochastic order, and mean R=2/3, mean R^2=1/2 give the exact second moment. Independently integrated conditional survival with Gauss quadrature for eight cases across all regimes; observed tail ratios approached the analytic constants (largest finite epsilon relative error ~12%, reducing epsilon improved all).

value.rationale: A classical singular metric cone has a natural intrinsic random-distance diameter; its near-maximal rare-event probability undergoes a geometric transition between apex-rim and rim-rim contact modes. final_claim: For independent area-uniform points on the closed lateral surface (not disk) of a right circular cone with slant length L and shape kappa=b/L in (0,1), the intrinsic diameter is L max(1,2sin(pi*kappa/2)). The upper-diameter tail is cubic with distinct explicit coefficients below, at, and above kappa=1/3; there is strict stochastic ordering and E[D^2]/L^2=1-8sin(pi*kappa)/(9*pi*kappa).
limitations: Closed lateral surface only, no filled-in base disk; two independent area-uniform points.
Fixed cone kappa and eps/L->0; no noncircular cones or moving-shape transition law.
